questions.problem: Consider the function $f(x)=\frac{x+10}{x+1}.$ Given that $y=f(x)$ is invertible throughout its domain, determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(4).$
questions.worked_solution:
To determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(4),$ we use the following formula:

$$
{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(4)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(4))}
$$

First, we calculate the value of ${f}^{-1}(4).$ To do this, we solve the equation ${f}^{-1}(4)=x.$ For $x\ne -1,$ this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{-1}(4) & =x \\ f(x) & =4 \\ \frac{x+10}{x+1} & =4 \\ \frac{x+10}{x+1}\cdot (x+1) & =4\cdot (x+1) \\ \frac{x+10}{\cancel{(x+1)}}\cdot \cancel{(x+1)} & =4x+4 \\ x+10 & =4x+4 \\ x & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{-1}(4)=2.$

Now we calculate ${f}^{′}(2),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{x+10}{x+1} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-\frac{9}{(x+1)^{2}} \\ {f}^{′}(2) & =-\frac{9}{{(2+1)}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{9}{{(3)}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{9}{9} \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(4) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(4))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(2)} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Consider the function $f(x)=8x-{x}^{4}$ and the point $P(1,7)$ that lies on $y=f(x).$ Given that $f(x)$ is invertible in the vicinity of $P,$ the slope of $y={f}^{-1}(x)$ at the point $(7,1)$ is$\,${{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
We start by calculating the derivative of $f$ at the point $(1,7).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}f(x) & =8x-{x}^{4} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =8-4{x}^{3} \\ {f}^{′}(1) & =4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $(1,7)$ lies on $y=f(x),$ we know that the corresponding point $(7,1)$ lies on $y={f}^{-1}(x).$

Furthermore, the slopes of the tangents to the two respective points are reciprocals. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(7) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(7))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
To determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(2),$ we use the following formula:

$$
{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(2)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(2))}
$$

First, we calculate the value of ${f}^{-1}(2).$ To do this, we solve the equation ${f}^{-1}(2)=x.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{-1}(2) & =x \\ f(x) & =2 \\ \sqrt{x} & =2 \\ x & ={2}^{2} \\ x & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have ${f}^{-1}(2)=4.$

Now, we calculate ${f}^{′}(4),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\sqrt{x} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} \\ {f}^{′}(4) & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{4}} \\ {f}^{′}(4) & =\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(2) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(2))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(4)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{4})} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
